name: Tinashe
description:
'''Tinashe Jorgensen Kachingwe''' ({{IPAc-en|t|iː|ˈ|n|ɑː|ʃ|eɪ|audio=LL-Q1860 (eng)-Flame, not lame-Tinashe.wav}} {{respell|tee|NAH|shay}}; born February 6, 1993) is an American singer, songwriter, dancer, and actress. Born in [[Lexington, Kentucky]], Tinashe moved to [[Pasadena, California]] to begin her career as a [[child actor]], before later expanding into music. From 2007 to 2011, she was a member of the girl group [[the Stunners]]. After the group disbanded, she released her first solo mixtapes: ''[[In Case We Die (Tinashe album)|In Case We Die]]'' (2012), ''[[Reverie (Tinashe album)|Reverie]]'' (2012), and ''[[Black Water (Tinashe album)|Black Water]]'' (2013).

After signing with [[RCA Records]], Tinashe released her debut studio album, ''[[Aquarius (Tinashe album)|Aquarius]]'' (2014), which marked her first appearance on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] with its lead single "[[2 On]]" (featuring [[Schoolboy Q]]). Her subsequent albums, ''[[Nightride (album)|Nightride]]'' (2016) and ''[[Joyride (Tinashe album)|Joyride]]'' (2018), peaked at number 89 and number 58, respectively, on the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]]. Following her departure from RCA, Tinashe released ''[[Songs for You]]'' (2019), ''[[333 (Tinashe album)|333]]'' (2021), and ''[[BB/Ang3l]]'' (2023) as an [[independent artist]], with all three albums failing to chart within the top 100. Her seventh studio album, ''[[Quantum Baby]]'' (2024), achieved moderate commercial success with the singles "[[Nasty (Tinashe song)|Nasty]]" and "[[No Broke Boys]]". Her eighth studio album, ''[[Popstar (Tinashe album)|Popstar]]'', became her first to reach the top ten in the United States.
